title: Food trailers built in Spencer through Midwest Concession Trailers - NewsBreak
text:
By Travis Chinn ,
1 days ago
SPENCER, Iowa ( KCAU ) — Midwest Concession Trailers started business in 2012.
“I had seen a niche where people were looking for these food trucks, concession trailers, and there weren’t a lot of places in the Midwest that were building them,” said Scott Pyle, Owner of Midwest Concession Trailers.
The company spent the next few years building food trucks and trailers locally until 2017.
“We had the opportunity to build what we call a midway trailer, which is a much larger, more grand, kind of elaborate food trailer,” said Pyle. “We built our first one and sent it out on the road, and other people saw it, and it’s kind of grown from there, and that’s really what we specialize in now.”
Every aspect of the trailer is done in-house, and it takes from four to seven weeks to build each trailer depending on the complexity.
Story continues below
Trailers can cost from $40,000 to $275,000.
“There’s a pretty broad spectrum based on the kind of equipment needs you have, and the size of the trailer and how elaborate the lighting is. The trailer behind me is seventeen feet tall when it’s all set up, and it’s got a folding marquee. They get fairly pricey,” added Pyle.
The company builds about ten new trailers a year and also remodels older trailers.
“A lot of the big manufacturers, they just build the new ones; they don’t want to mess with the remodel stuff. That’s been a big market for us,” said Pyle.
And the company has grown from two employees to twelve since its start
“It’s different every day. You’re not doing the same thing every day. You finish one project, you go to the next. Today I’m working on probably eight different things. I’m not doing the same thing,” said Sam Van Lenning, Shop Foreman at Midwest Concession Trailers.
And hopefully the demand for food trailers continues.
“I feel like the industry has been consistent, and I think it’s going to stay consistent, and I think that the demand for trailers will always be there,” said Pyle.
Midwest Concession Trailers are all over the United States and even one in Canada.
